assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules. Closely-related concerns may share one method (e.g. fulfillment type and delivery address, which follow the same 'same shipment iff same type and address' rule), so four methods covering five concerns is fine. FAILS only when a single method carries all the rules; PASSES with two or more concern-focused methods.
assertions.evidence: [split vote 2/3 pass] Four @TableTest methods: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress, splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability, choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount, keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. Judge each @TableTest table independently; the assertion FAILS if any table meets any of these conditions: (1) its expectation column holds the same value in every row; (2) in every row, each expectation cell is a verbatim copy of a cell in an input column of the same row; (3) an implementation that ignored the input columns entirely and returned a fixed value would satisfy every row. Otherwise the assertion PASSES. Do not fail a table merely because its values are simple or round — only these three conditions matter.
assertions.evidence: [split vote 2/3 pass] Fulfillment table: same items produce [camera,lens] vs different addresses produce [camera, watch]. Availability: IN_STOCK produces IMMEDIATE vs BACKORDERED produces WHEN_AVAILABLE. Warehouse: single cover [W1:...] vs split [W1:..., W2:...]

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body. The assertion FAILS if any of these hold for any @TableTest: (1) a value needed to predict the expectation (a threshold, rate, cutoff, multiplier, reference date) appears only in the method body or a field, and in neither a column, the @DisplayName, nor the @Description; (2) the operation applied to the inputs cannot be named from the column headers and cell values alone; (3) a helper method used in the assertion applies a comparison criterion (ordering, tolerance, subset matching) that is stated nowhere in the table, title, or description. Otherwise the assertion PASSES. Setup that merely constructs the objects named by the columns is not a failure.
assertions.evidence: [split vote 2/3 pass] @Description blocks state key assumptions: 'BACKORDERED and PRE_ORDERED both ship WHEN_AVAILABLE', 'fewest-shipments combination must be chosen', 'Companions only affect outcome when multiple warehouse combinations tie'

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods. All outputs of the same concern belong together.
assertions.evidence: Each method has single Shipments? output column. Warehouse and companion methods include both warehouse assignment and shipment count in one Shipments? column via describeByWarehouse

assertions.text: A compound output — a collection of items, or items keyed by a tag — is expressed as a native TableTest list, map, or set (possibly nested, e.g. [[a, b], [c]] or [W1: [a, b]]), not as a hand-rolled string that encodes the structure with embedded brackets or colons (e.g. "W1:[a,b]") and is assembled or parsed by a helper. FAILS when an expectation cell packs multiple values into one quoted scalar that the test builds via a stringifying helper. PASSES when the output column is a native collection — sets for order-independent semantics, or ordered lists/maps with a canonical sort. Scalar outputs (a number, an enum, or a single message) are exempt.
assertions.evidence: Expected shipments use string encoding like ["W1:[camera,lens,mic]"] and ["IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]"] built by describeByWarehouse/describeByAvailability helpers, not native TableTest collections like [W1: {camera, lens, mic}].
